notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, as the county reported them in its F-65 Annual Local Unit Fiscal Report to the Michigan Department of Treasury. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.

Spending is reported by function for the general fund, other governmental funds, enterprise funds (water, sewer and other utilities) and component units (such as downtown development authorities). Capital outlay has no function, so enterprise capital counts as utilities and the rest is spread over the other spending in proportion.
Component units are included: the county road commission and other authorities the county appoints and funds.
Internal service funds ($24,088,079 of their revenue and spending) are left out, since the departments they serve report that spending.
Borrowing, transfers between funds, sales of capital assets, depreciation and extraordinary items are left out.
General government, courts, community and economic development, and redevelopment and public housing count as overhead.
Debt is total long-term debt at year end, as reported on the F-65.
Political money is not scored: Michigan county candidates file campaign finance reports with their county clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Michigan yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Face recognition
redFlags.detail: The Grand Traverse County Sheriff's Office has desktop access to Michigan State Police's face recognition system, the Statewide Network of Agency Photos (SNAP).

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS010264, citing Michigan State Police

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Grand Traverse County Sheriff's Office operates one DJI Phantom drone as of 2015, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003325, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: As of April 2024, the Grand Traverse County Sheriff's Office operates 28 Flock Safety automated license plate readers. The agency stores ALPR data for 30 days.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS011619, citing Flock Safety

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Grand Traverse County and the township the village is part of.
Village residents also pay the township the village is part of, which is listed separately.

Spending is reported by function for the general fund, other governmental funds, enterprise funds (water, sewer and other utilities) and component units (such as downtown development authorities). Capital outlay has no function, so enterprise capital counts as utilities and the rest is spread over the other spending in proportion.
Internal service funds ($143,753 of their revenue and spending) are left out, since the departments they serve report that spending.
Borrowing, transfers between funds, sales of capital assets, depreciation and extraordinary items are left out.
General government, courts, community and economic development, and redevelopment and public housing count as overhead.
Debt is total long-term debt at year end, as reported on the F-65.
Political money is not scored: Michigan local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside Village of Fife Lake's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-18.

A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Michigan yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
